doc_name: List of aftershocks of the April 2015 Nepal earthquake
text: After the main earthquake in Nepal on 25 April 2015, there was some seismic activity in the Jumla district prior to the main shock, but these events are not considered foreshocks. As of 7 June 2015, over 304 aftershocks had occurred, a number that seismologists describe as normal. Seismologist Roger Musson notes that the typical pattern for aftershocks is that the largest one occurs one day after the main shock and is one magnitude less. Thus, the 6.7 magnitude aftershock on 26 April 2015, following the 7.8 magnitude main shock, aligns with this pattern. It is highly unlikely that the earthquake was a foreshock to a larger future event, and therefore, an earthquake exceeding 7.8 magnitude is not expected in the near future after 25 April 2015. The list provided below is incomplete and may contain inaccuracies, and it includes only significant earthquakes.
